likelihood.contr

Compose likelihood models from heterogeneous observation types.

Many real datasets mix exact observations with censored ones. A sensor might record a precise failure time or only that a unit survived past inspection. Each observation type contributes differently to the log-likelihood, but they share the same parameters. likelihood.contr lets you declare each type’s contribution separately, then compose them into a single model with full inference support: MLE, standard errors, confidence intervals, likelihood ratio tests, and Fisher information.

Installation 

# From r-universe
install.packages("likelihood.contr",
                 repos = "https://queelius.r-universe.dev")

# Or from GitHub
remotes::install_github("queelius/likelihood.contr")

Quick Example

Fit a Weibull model to a mix of exact and right-censored failure times:

library(likelihood.contr)
library(likelihood.model)

# Define model: Weibull with two observation types
model <- likelihood_contr(
  obs_type = "status",
  exact = contr_name("weibull", "exact", ob_col = "t"),
  right = contr_name("weibull", "right", ob_col = "t")
)

# Simulate data with 50% censoring
set.seed(42)
raw <- rweibull(300, shape = 2, scale = 5)
df <- data.frame(
  t      = pmin(raw, 4),
  status = ifelse(raw <= 4, "exact", "right")
)

# Fit and inspect
result <- fit(model)(df, par = c(shape = 1.5, scale = 4))
summary(result)
#> Coefficients:
#>       Estimate Std. Error   2.5% 97.5%
#> shape   2.0672     0.1611 1.7514 2.383
#> scale   4.9571     0.2309 4.5046 5.410

Three lines to define the model. One line to fit it. Full asymptotic inference for free.

How It Works

likelihood.contr provides two contribution constructors:

  • contr_name() builds contributions from any R distribution ("norm", "exp", "weibull", …) for exact, right-censored, left-censored, or interval-censored data.
  • contr_fn() wraps user-supplied log-likelihood, score, and Hessian functions for custom observation types.

likelihood_contr() composes these into a model that implements the likelihood.model interface: loglik(), score(), hess_loglik(), fit(), lrt(), fim(), and more.
